idiom_name: tower-sessions SessionManagerLayer over a SessionStore (MemoryStore, Redis via fred, SQLx stores)
implementation_notes: tower-sessions brings the pattern to tower/axum applications: SessionManagerLayer::new(store) installs session handling as a layer, the Session extractor gives handlers a typed key/value interface over serde types, and persistence is delegated to any type implementing the SessionStore trait - MemoryStore for tests and single-instance servers, or maintained Redis, SQLx, MongoDB, Sled and DynamoDB stores for a farm. The design deliberately loads a session from its backing store only when a handler actually touches it, and CachingSessionStore can put a local cache in front of the canonical store, which is the crate's answer to the per-request round trip; expiry (for example Expiry::OnInactivity) is configured on the layer.
pitfalls: MemoryStore is per process and does not survive a restart, so it cannot back a horizontally scaled deployment; stores without automatic expiry (SQLx, MongoDB) need a continuous deletion task or the table grows.
Session values must be Serialize/Deserialize and owned; references to request-scoped data cannot be stored, and the extractor's rejection has to be handled in the handler signature.
Loading is lazy, so a handler that never touches Session pays nothing - but code that assumes the record was loaded eagerly will be wrong about when the store was consulted.
